sections.html:
Florence, the seat of Florence County, had 39,899 residents in 2020, which made it the tenth largest city in South Carolina. Its 23.49 square miles sit in the coastal plain of the northeast. Hospitals set the tone for the local job market: McLeod Regional Medical Center is the largest employer in the Pee Dee region, and MUSC Florence ranks third.

Interstate 20 ends here and Interstate 95 runs through town, and Florence Regional Airport lies about 2 miles east of downtown. Those links make it easy for an owner who lives elsewhere to run a sale remotely.

sections.h2: Who bills property tax inside the city limits
sections.html:
One county bill covers everything. Florence County collects real estate and personal property tax on behalf of the City of Florence, and the city's levy is folded into that bill. Each year City Council fixes the millage by June 30, ahead of the July 1 to June 30 fiscal year.

Vehicles, watercraft, aircraft and business personal property are the Florence County Auditor's responsibility. Bills are mailed to the last address the county has, and an owner who never receives one still owes the tax. That makes the Tax Assessor's Office the place to report any change in where mail should go.

The county offices keep weekday hours, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. For the city's side of the story, read its property tax payments page.

January 15 is the deadline for real estate tax. State law, in Section 12-45-180, then layers on 3 percent on January 16, another 7 percent on February 2 and another 5 percent on March 17. The sum is 15 percent plus collection costs.

Notices tend to arrive around October. If January 15 falls on a weekend or holiday, the deadline generally slides to the next business day. Payment options are a visit to the county complex, a check mailed to 180 N Irby Street, or the county's PayStar portal. The city cautions against mailing cash, and the county answers mailed payments with a receipt by mail.

There is a narrow break for ownership changes. If a house changes hands during the tax year, the notice reached only the old owner and the new one had none in time, the treasurer shall waive penalties. Few sellers qualify, so do not plan around it.

sections.h2: What a seller can do about an assessment
sections.html:
Dispute a value with a written objection to the assessor, sent within 90 days after the assessment notice is mailed. The assessor must send a notice whenever it raises a value by $1,000 or more, and in a reassessment year those notices are due by October 1. Without a notice you may still appeal in writing at any time, but the appeal only counts for the current year if you file before the first penalty date.

The county reappraises every five years and holds a parcel's increase to 15 percent over that span unless an assessable transfer of interest occurs. When values rise overall, millage is rolled back. Written appeals go to the Assessor's office, which also provides a PDF form. Call 843-665-3056 to ask which cycle and dates apply to your parcel.

sections.h2: If taxes on a Florence house go unpaid
sections.html:
Florence County may take unpaid real property and mobile home taxes to a public sale. Charges start building before then. Recent amounts include $20 for notices in March, $30 for certified mail of a levy in April, $25 for advertising in August and $60 for a land mortgage search in October.

The latest sale was set for October 5, 2026 in the parking garage at the County Complex. An owner or a mortgage holder has one year and a day to redeem, and interest rises in quarterly steps at 3, 6, 9 and 12 percent of the bid. Solid waste fees that are past due add $25 when paid after March 16. A tax deed is not a warranty deed, and the county says liens can remain.

sections.h2: Selling a Florence house that owes tax
sections.html:
Owing tax does not rule out a sale. Call 843-665-3095 for the payoff figure before you fix a closing date, then ask your title company to list that figure on the settlement statement.

  1. Get the payoff. Penalties step up in January, February and March, and costs rise during the year, so a stale number can be wrong.
  2. Ask the Assessor to confirm where your bills are mailed.
  3. If your loan is escrowed, check with the mortgage holder about what it has already paid.
  4. Ask the City Finance Department at 843-665-3162 how the city's share appears on the bill.

If the house has sat vacant or has deferred repairs, a cash sale can close without the repair list and showings of a retail listing. We buy houses as they are, and we need only the address and your latest tax notice to start.

Summers in Florence are long, hot and humid, so buyers' inspectors spend their time on the cooling system, attic ventilation and the roof. They test the air conditioner and look for water stains. Moisture in a crawlspace is another practical concern. Servicing the cooling equipment and fixing small roof leaks before you list is cheaper than negotiating a credit later.

Gather service receipts for the roof and the air conditioner, and keep them with the tax notice and payoff letter. A clean folder tells buyers and their lenders that the house has been looked after and that the tax picture is clear.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax for the City of Florence?
faqs.a: Florence County does. The County Treasurer collects City of Florence real estate and personal property taxes on the same county bill.

faqs.q: When is the property tax deadline in Florence, SC?
faqs.a: January 15. A 3 percent penalty starts January 16, and more is added on February 2 and March 17, for 15 percent in total plus costs.

faqs.q: Who sets the city's property tax rate?
faqs.a: City Council sets the millage by June 30 for the July 1 to June 30 fiscal year. You pay it on the county bill.

faqs.q: What if I never received a Florence tax bill?
faqs.a: You still owe the tax. Bills go to the owner's last known address, so keep the Tax Assessor's Office up to date on where mail goes.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Florence house if I owe taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, but the balance and any fees must be cleared. Call the Delinquent Tax Office at 843-665-3095 for a payoff figure before you set a closing date.
